name: Question 17
problem:
In a factory, cans are filled with soda. The amount of soda in one can is normally distributed with a mean of $340\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $4\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$ The weight of a can is normally distributed with a mean of $25\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $1\,{\text{g}}^{2}$ If one can containing soda is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs more than $360\,\text{g}?$ You may assume that the weights of soda and cans are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-2.3\,$ | $\,0.0102\,$ | $\,0.0099\,$ | $\,0.0096\,$ | $\,0.0094\,$ |
| $\,-2.2\,$ | $\,0.0132\,$ | $\,0.0129\,$ | $\,0.0125\,$ | $\,0.0122\,$ |
| $\,-2.1\,$ | $\,0.0170\,$ | $\,0.0166\,$ | $\,0.0162\,$ | $\,0.0158\,$ |
worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the weight of the soda, and let $Y$ denote the weight of the can. We want to find 

$$
P(X+Y>360).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables such that $X∼N(340,4)$ and $Y∼N(25,1)$, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}X+Y & ∼N(340+25,4+1) \\  & ∼N(365,5).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variable $X+Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =365$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{5}.$

In order to find $P(X+Y>360),$ we convert $X+Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>360) & =P(Z>\frac{360-365}{\sqrt{5}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-2.24) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -2.24) \\  & =1-Φ(-2.24)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-2.24)≈0.0125.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>360) & ≈1-Φ(-2.24) \\  & ≈1-0.0125 \\  & ≈0.9875.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that the probability that a randomly selected can with soda weighs more than $360$ grams is $0.9875.$
